For how much time I spend online, I know basically nothing about computers/infoseq/programming. What are some free resources I can use to learn some practical skills?

If you want to learn about network security, securely communicating between machines, or anything computer related, you can "play" one of the many wargames online.

Personally, I like the ones from OverTheWire. They start you off as basically as you can get (with Bandit) and bring you up to speed pretty quickly.

One word of advice, though: there are "walkthroughs" online designed to "help" you out when you're in a jam... DON'T USE THEM! OverTheWire actually lists multiple commands you may or may not need for every "level," and it's up to you to read the man pages and learn what each of those commands do, and how to use them. It's up to you to know/learn how to actually implement those commands to progress to the next "level."
If you want to learn programming, khan academy or codeacademy are both great resources.
